thread:
Maya: Heads-up from the Private preview runs: long responses come back with a single final HTTP body instead of streaming chunks. Our probe-client and the canary harness are currently marking these as failures. Need a short-term compatibility plan and a long-term handshake to avoid surprises.
Asif: Is this an adapter limitation or something at the runtime driver level?
Maya: Mostly adapter. The Private sidecar didn't implement the streaming manifest we expected. The control plane probe assumes streaming unless told otherwise.
Toni: Can we add an explicit capability blob in the probe handshake? Small, versioned, and non-breaking. Then routers and clients can make decisions.
Sam: That would be ideal. We also need to account for Dedicated which streams but uses different chunk sizes. The contract should include chunk semantics.
Asif: Proposal: handshake includes handshake_version:int and capabilities:{ streaming_mode:string, max_chunk_size:int, fallback_policy:string }. streaming_mode can be one of [none, immediate, buffered].
Maya: Nice. "none" = no streaming, "immediate" = stream chunks as produced, "buffered" = runtime buffers until first token boundary then emits. Backcompat: missing field => none.
Toni: Make handshake opt-in: only runtimes that want to opt into richer semantics add the field. That keeps older adapters working without changes.
Sam: Router change: when request requires streaming, prefer runtimes with streaming_mode in [immediate, buffered] and prefer immediate over buffered. If none available, route to host/dedicated with X-Fallback-Reason:streaming_unavailable and log a quality event.
Asif: Also add a small capability validator on registration so operator gets alerted if they claim immediate but tests show buffered behavior.
Maya: Client/probe changes: before starting a stream, probe checks handshake.capabilities.streaming_mode. If none => switch to polling path (probe_v1). If buffered => start stream but track first-token latency metric.
Toni: Console/UI: surface canary degradation states: STREAM_OK, STREAM_BUFFERED, STREAM_FALLBACK. These map to our metrics and alert rules.
Sam: Tests I'll add: routing predicate unit tests and an integration with two fake runtimes showing immediate vs buffered behavior so we can validate metrics and fallback headers. Pseudo: 
```py
def test_stream_routing_prefers_immediate():
  req = Request(streaming=True)
  runtimes = [R(streaming_mode='buffered'), R(streaming_mode='immediate')]
  assert route(req, runtimes).streaming_mode == 'immediate'
```
Asif: Edge case: quantized kernels may advertise immediate but still produce first-byte delay. Add a streaming_quality enum or a measured flag runtime reports (estimated_first_byte_ms). We should not make routing brittle on best-effort numbers; prefer modes and then use measured telemetry to tune.
Maya: Agreed. Keep handshake simple but allow optional numeric hints: estimated_first_byte_ms. Routers ignore numeric hints for selection but console surfaces them for ops.
Toni: Migration notes: Private adapters will need a tiny shim to populate handshake fields. We'll add a one-week grace period where probe tolerates missing capability and logs a deprecation warning.
deploy-bot: Staging rollout (router + probe) passed smoke tests :tada:
Maya: Action items: Asif to open adapter PR (handshake fields + optional hints) ETA 48h. Sam to update router predicate + tests ETA 48h. Toni to draft console copy + canary states ETA 72h. Maya will update probe harness and add integration tests ETA 72h.
Asif: I'll also add an ops check that flags runtimes claiming immediate if first-byte p50 > 200ms for two consecutive hours.
Sam: I'll produce a minimal PoC tomorrow that fakes two runtimes so QA can validate canary UX.
Maya: Thanks. This should prevent silent quality regressions across hosted/dedicated/private. :thumbsup:
